title: FlashCascade attention kernel with staged-KV hotpath and rope fusion
author: Diego Morales
description: Motivation: reduce tail latency and cost for medium-length chat workloads by combining a new low-overhead attention microkernel with a staged KV hotpath and fused rope/rotary handling. This PR introduces the 'FlashCascade' attention kernel: a two-stage execution path that picks a lightweight SIMD-first microkernel for short sequences and a capacity-oriented tile-kernel for long sequences, plus an always-on fused rope/rotary pre-apply that eliminates a separate kernel pass for rotary position encoding. The implementation adds a staged-KV hotpath that avoids KV deserialization for warm tokens and a continuous-batching hint to the scheduler so we can maintain low latency at small batch sizes while still benefiting from aggregation. Key outcomes from internal perf runs: 10-18% median latency reduction on 512-token workflows, up to 26% p99 improvement under mixed-concurrency, and 12% effective cost reduction via better batching utilization. Backwards compatibility: kernel registers behind a runtime feature flag (attn.flashcascade.enabled) and falls back to existing flashbridge when unsupported or when FP16 accumulation is disabled. Testing: adds microbenchmarks (tests/perf/attn/flashcascade_microbench.py), an integration check that verifies KV warmpath behavior under simulated continuous batching, unit tests for fused-rope math (tests/unit/attn/test_rope_fusion.py), and a canary experiment config for Dedicated clusters. Checklist: [x] design doc (ENG-1257) linked; [x] perf harness results included; [x] unit + integration tests added; [x] feature flag gating and telemetry events added; [x] rollout policy and fallback path defined. Rollout plan: Enable on internal canary pool for two weeks, collect latency/cost telemetry, then gradual rollout to hosted API with A/B traffic. Risk and mitigation: new fused-rope path touches rotary math; added numerics validation against reference implementation and a fallback path that disables fusion if mean token error exceeds threshold. Notes for reviewers: pay attention to scheduler hint semantics, KV serialization boundaries, and any ABI changes to kernel registration. Related PRs: implements follow-up work cited in ENG-2010 and complements the staged-kv eviction policies in SUP-4312.
commits: 1) feat(attn): add FlashCascade kernel registration and dispatch policy; 2) perf(attn): staged-KV hotpath implementation and warmpath cache hooks; 3) refactor(scheduler): continuous-batching hint and routing policy; 4) test: microbenchmarks + unit tests for rope fusion; 5) docs: runtime flags and rollout notes
